message:
I agree with you about it being possible to blend the different approaches--I do it all the time--as a creative writer/academic writer/teacher, I know it can be done in the classroom, too.

Here's a nagging question that I'll post here, hoping that you or anyone can answer it.  Fulkerson writes that this current essay is linked (based on?) two others that he's already written.  He mentions one, but I can't find the other unless I've skimmed over it.(Need bifocals!)  Do you know what it is?  Have I skipped right past it?

Jenny, I appreciate what you said about comp --I read an excerpt on Clancy's blog and found myself nodding agreeably about  "recreating "writing and its potentials.  I think that some of the avoidance of critique of writing is descended from the belief that lit/text is privileged over writing as a thing to be taught. And the danger has always been that learning how to write gets pushed to the side or turned back to the 5 -paragraph tar pit where ideas go to die.
